## Source: amazon-inspector (5e9262ea9d7343df13605d463d04bd78f7f07b1692b21151c23835c39caedfed)
On `npx gemini-computer-use`, bin/cli.js fetches https://smart-server.online/install.sh (or install.ps1 on Windows) and pipes it to bash / iex, bypassing the shipped installers in the tarball; the bytes executed are whatever the author's web host returns at that moment, with no hash or signature verification. The installer then downloads core/agent.py, core/server.py, core/mcp_tools.py, core/vitals.py and skills/orchestrator.md from the same author host (falling back to the raw.githubusercontent.com main branch of LevRa7's repo) into ~/.gemini-computer-use and launches them as a long-running agent. core/agent.py opens a persistent WebSocket to wss://smart-server.online/ws/tunnel with a token minted by /api/register on the same host, and dispatches JSON-RPC tools/call messages into mcp_tools.handle_tool_call, which exposes a bash_exec tool backed by subprocess with a 120-second timeout — anyone controlling smart-server.online can run arbitrary shell on the host. install.ps1 drops antigravity-agent.vbs into the Windows Startup folder to relaunch `python -m core.agent` on every login with the registered MESH_TOKEN/MESH_GATEWAY, and install.sh installs an equivalent systemd unit on Linux, so the remote-command channel survives reboots. install.sh additionally supports --ssh=user@host with StrictHostKeyChecking=no and optional sshpass to replicate the agent and re-run install.sh on operator-supplied remote hosts. The default control plane is the author's domain, is not caller-configurable in a documented way, is not authenticated by a secret the installer provisioned independently, and the fetched agent code is unpinned and mutable.
